title: Pouring Of First Concrete Begins For Nuclear Island At China’s Sanao-4
summary: First concrete pouring has begun for the nuclear island of Unit 4 at the Sanao nuclear power station in eastern Chinese province of Zhejiang, project owner China General Nuclear (CGN) announced on Tuesday (10 November). The company said the pouring of first concrete began at 08:28 local time on 10 November, marking the official start of main construction. It said the total volume of concrete poured as of 10 November was approximately 8,820 cubic metres and the process is expected to last 60 hours.

title: Atomic spectroscopy used to resolve one nuclear size anomaly and reveal another
summary: Researchers have used a new approach to measure differences in the sizes of atomic nuclei, resolving a longstanding discrepancy while uncovering a new finding that current nuclear theories cannot fully explain. The size of an atomic nucleus, measured by its nuclear charge radius, provides information about how protons and neutrons are arranged within it and is used to understand nuclear structure and deformation.

title: Springtime for the full nuclear fuel cycle
summary: Craig Piercycpiercy@ans.org The Trump administration’s Department of Energy has done good. Its Nuclear Lifecycle Innovation Campuses (NLIC) initiative has planted some important seeds that are starting to sprout. Five states—Idaho, Louisiana, Oklahoma, Tennessee, and Utah—have found the courage to pull out a map, put a finger on a spot, and say, “This place is worth exploring for nuclear waste disposal.” Of course, these states aren’t looking only at the economic benefits of disposal. They see the larger prize: becoming a hub for recycling, front-end fuel cycle facilities, and advanced reactor development and services. Some in the nuclear community worry that the near-term economic impact of recycling has been oversold to these states, a byproduct of the irrational exuberance of a few. But I suspect that if you polled ANS’s nearly 13,000 members, most would say we’ll be recycling at least some of our nuclear fuel within a few decades. Across the nuclear community, there’s a growing sense that recycling is not an option anymore—it’s an eventuality. The real question is how to get there. What is the path?

title: UK Nuclear Professionals Confident, But Warn Of Uncertainties And Challenges
summary: Nuclear professionals are confident about the future of the UK industry, but warn that funding uncertainty, skills shortages and challenges delivering major projects could hamper its growth, according to new research from the Nuclear Institute. A survey of Nuclear Institute members found that almost four in five (79.7%) respondents are optimistic about the industry’s future, with a third of these (33.3%) describing themselves as very optimistic. However, the research also highlighted concerns over the industry’s ability to turn ambition into action, with respondents identifying project costs, workforce capacity, regulatory barriers and long-term government support among its most pressing challenges.

title: Estonia Shortlists Three Locations For First BWRX-300 Nuclear Power Plant
summary: Estonia said it will now focus on three potential locations in the Viru-Nigula region in the north of the country for the development of its first nuclear power plants having discarded three sites for what it called “national security reasons”. In a statement, the Estonian government said that the Madala, Malla and Letipea sites would be the three sites considered to host Estonia-based project development company Fermi Energia’s planned development of two 300-MW GE Vernova Hitachi Nuclear Energy BWRX-300 small modular reactors (SMRs). Three sites in Lüganuse municipality, also in the north of the country, were excluded from plans due to national defence reasons, a decision based on assessment guidelines outlined by the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) for the risk profile of sites.
